newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng leaps in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng leaps in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped 191 points, 1.55 percent, to 12,533 just after the Wednesday morning open, prompted by a benign U.S. inflation data figures and a strong rebound on Wall Street, brokers said.
The index continued to climb, putting on 220 points, or 1.78 percent, to 12,562 in the first 10 minutes of trade.
"The index could test the 12,600 level," said Peter Lai, sales director at OCBC Securities.
But he forecast the index should consolidate after that.
"At this moment, there can't be any breakthrough because there must be a consolidation in the (physical) property market," Lai added.
The market was unlikely to break out of its medium-term trading range, he said.

Brokers said the market's surge was in line with Wall Street's strong rally overnight. The Dow Industrials leaped 135.26 points or 2.1 percent to 6,587.16 following the release of benign inflation data in the U.S. consumer price index for March.
But the property sector led the market's early rally, followed by property-based issues in the commercial and industrial sector.
Cheung Kong led the property sector with a jump of HK$1.50 to HK66.00, and Hutchison Whampoa led the conglomerates, advancing HK$1.00 to HK$56.50.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings, the most actively traded issue, jumped HK$3.00 to HK$185.50 on trade of HK$111.84 million.
Market turnover after 25 minutes was a robust HK$1.5 billion.
The April Hang Seng Index contract added 237 points to 12,532 and May followed with a gain of 230 points to 12,515.
Some see the Hang Seng returning to the 13,000 level in the near term.
"We will reach 12,800 to 13,000 in the next week or two," said Tony Measor at Dharmala Securities.
The reason people have been selling the Hong Kong market is because New York is bad, not because Hong Kong is bad, he said.
